title: Complete Structural Determination of Mesostructural Dodecagonal Quasicrystalline Particles
authors: Xueliang Zhang, Xi Wang, Nobuhisa Fujita, Osamu Terasaki, Lu Han
abstract: Quasicrystals have revolutionized our understanding of order in solids by demonstrating exotic structural and physicochemical properties with diverse potential applications. Despite the development of various theoretical models and experimental techniques to describe quasicrystal structures, the precise determination of local three dimensional (3D) arrangements of constituent atoms, or of secondary building units such as clusters or micelles, remains elusive. This challenge is particularly acute in self assembled soft matter quasicrystalline systems, where the complex assembly of molecular groups introduces additional defects and structural modulations. Herein, we report the first complete structural determination of self-assembled mesostructural dodecagonal quasicrystalline particles. Employing advanced electron tomography, combined with dedicated structural tracing and processing workflows, the 3D coordinates of all nodal sites were extracted. This approach reveals that the actual structure deviates from the conventionally assumed tetrahedral close packing geometry, exhibiting diverse coordination environments and displacive fluctuations. We identified and quantified rotational intergrowths arising from node exchange, as well as various defects and disorder, with these features discernible only through 3D analysis. Additionally, we propose a simplified two-layer stacking of isomorphic hexagonal model to form dodecagonal quasicrystal. This work advances our understanding of soft-matter dodecagonal quasicrystals and paves the way for detailed structural elucidation of self-assembled systems.
summary: This work presents the first complete 3D structural determination of self-assembled mesostructural dodecagonal quasicrystals using advanced electron tomography. By analyzing nodal sites, the authors revealed that the structure deviates from simple theoretical models, quantifying defects and fluctuations. This advances understanding of soft-matter quasiperiodic order by providing detailed atomic-scale structural data.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving a precise, local three-dimensional (3D) structural determination of constituent atoms or secondary building units within complex self-assembled soft matter quasicrystalline systems.
main_result: The study reports the first complete 3D structure of mesostructural dodecagonal quasicrystals, revealing that the actual arrangement deviates from ideal tetrahedral close packing and exhibits quantifiable defects and fluctuations.
method: Advanced electron tomography was employed to acquire tilt-series data, followed by custom structural tracing workflows to extract 3D coordinates of nodal sites across the entire particle volume.
model_or_system: The physical system is self-assembled mesostructural dodecagonal quasicrystalline particles formed from cationic surfactant and silica precursors. The analysis compares the experimental structure against idealized models, such as the Tetrahedrally Close-Packed (TCP) lattice.
key_observables: 3D nodal coordinates, coordination numbers (CN), phason strain parameters ($\lambda$, $d$), and comparison of simulated vs. experimental TEM images.
important_parameters: The periodicity along the stacking axis (e.g., 6.9 nm for QC-1) and the cutoff distance used for neighbor counting ($1.5 	imes$ mean nearest-neighbor distance).
main_assumptions: Initial reconstruction assumes a spherical geometry for each extracted node, although subsequent analysis incorporates positional fluctuations to refine this.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the entire process: 2D tiling patterns, 3D tomogram reconstructions showing 12-fold symmetry in FFT, and direct comparisons between simulated TEM images based on derived models (Ideal vs. Fluctuated) and experimental views.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the structural challenge to detailing the advanced electron tomography data acquisition and reconstruction process. It then analyzes the extracted 3D nodal positions by classifying node types, quantifying deviations from ideal lattices using displacement analysis, and finally proposing a simplified two-layer stacking model that best fits the observed disorder.
why_interesting: While focused on materials science crystallography rather than fundamental quantum phenomena, the rigorous use of advanced tomography to resolve local structural details and quantify deviations from idealized periodic models (like TCP) shares methodological parallels with characterizing complex many-body ground states or defect structures in condensed matter theory.
